**Background and strategy**
- Secondary, inconsistent bios say he was born in Purisai, Tamil Nadu, in about 1964, has a postgraduate degree in mathematics, and taught math in Gujarat and then Singapore (1993–2005). They say he began trading in 2007 and specialised in selling OTM puts, later becoming known for options selling and theta capture. One source gives a conflicting 1982/engineer/Cognizant biography. Treat all of this as low-reliability — [ISFM](https://isfm.co.in/p-r-sundar-scam/); [WeRiseByLiftingOthers](https://www.werisebyliftingothers.in/2024/04/journey-of-trader-p-r-sundar.html)
- His YouTube channel has about 1.2 million subscribers, and he runs paid options workshops and an "Options Conclave" — [ISFM](https://isfm.co.in/p-r-sundar-net-worth/); [prsundar.com Options Conclave](http://prsundar.com/optionsconclave/)
- His own claims (X, Aug 2023): "I always discourage people with tiny capital doing Options Trading". He says he once made 100% in a year but has "also made losses sometimes", and that he considers "25-30% as very good returns" — [PRSundar64 on X](https://x.com/PRSundar64/status/1696158361501261954)
- Evidence of tail exposure, from his own tweet in Jan 2020: "Lost 15 lakhs as I sold Call options yesterday… ended with 9 lakh profit after wiping out all losses" — [PRSundar64 on X](https://twitter.com/PRSundar64/status/1215213725033984000)
- An anonymous critic alleges that a follower lost 74% of capital in two days selling Infosys options as Sundar suggested on YouTube. This is an unverified allegation — [Medium, tradingquacks](https://medium.com/@tradingquacks/how-an-acquaintance-lost-74-of-his-capital-in-just-2-days-by-selling-infosys-options-as-suggested-2b291b6282ad)
- A transcript collection includes his description of the COVID crash (Nifty down about 40%) and a stop-loss exit of about ₹2.82 lakh on one trade. The trade's date is not shown — [Kaggle transcripts](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/prayushkale/few-pr-sundar-transcripts). His blog's March 2020 archive has only market commentary — [prsundar.blogspot.com/2020/03](https://prsundar.blogspot.com/2020/03/)

   DRHP, SEBI order for ~1,500 small caps, every quarter.

   Indian parts supplier like Uniparts) — found on purpose, not by accident.

unless verified, no proprietary data.

1. Management promise tracker database (quarterly, whole small-cap universe) — the moat

   guidance hits/misses, auditor changes).

`case_study:netflix-2002-2025` · tickers US-NFLX · confidence: verified

IPO May 2002 at $15. Splits 2:1 (2004), 7:1 (2015), 10:1 (Nov 17 2025) = 140x, so IPO ~$0.11 on today's basis. Crash 1 (Qwikster): July 2011 peak ~$305 pre-2015-split (~$4.35 today) -> Sept 2012 low ~$53 (~$0.76), about -80%; AP: -75% from mid-July to Dec 2011, $12bn wiped, ~800k-2m subs lost after a ~60% price hike plus the plan to split DVD into 'Qwikster' (reversed in ~3 weeks). Crash 2: Nov 2021 ~$701 (~$70) -> May 2022 ~$163 (~$16), -76%, after the first subscriber loss in a decade. Then password-sharing crackdown + ad tier (ads >50% of signups where offered; ad revenue doubled 2024) -> >300m subs end-2024, stock >$1,000 for most of 2025 (~$110-134 post-split). IPO->2025 peak ~1,000x+; 2012 trough->2025 ~150x+. Rerating split: 2012-21 mostly revenue growth on very high P/E; 2022-25 mostly EPS growth (operating margin ~20% -> ~30%) [margins unverified]. EARLY SIGNAL at each trough: streaming hours and international sub adds kept rising while the stock collapsed; the error was self-inflicted pricing/communication, not demand. Who caught it: Carl Icahn disclosed ~10% in Oct 2012 near the low and made >$1bn [from memory, unverified]. LESSON: when a structurally winning platform crashes on a fixable management error, the drawdown is the opportunity; you must be able to sit through -75% twice.

- **Start → end:** $15 IPO = ~$0.11 split-adj → ~$110-134 (2025, post 10:1) (~1,000x IPO->2025; ~150x from 2012 low)
- **EPS vs rerating:** 2022-25 mostly EPS; P/E compressed in 2022 then partially re-expanded
- **Max drawdown:** ~-80% (2011-12), -76% (2021-22)
- **Early signal:** engagement/sub growth intact during crashes; errors fixable
- **Who caught it:** Carl Icahn 2012 [unverified]
- **Ended/stalled:** not ended as of 2025; post-split range
- **Lesson:** self-inflicted crashes in a winning platform are buyable; survive the drawdown
- **Sources:** [1](https://cases.som.yale.edu/netflix-and-qwikster) · [2](https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2011/oct/25/netflix-shares-tank-amid-backlash-and-defections/) · [3](https://techcrunch.com/2011/10/24/reed-hastings-qwikster-symbol-not-listening) · [4](https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/highly-anticipated-stock-split-will-take-effect-nov-17-heres-what-investors-need-know) · [5](https://finviz.com/news/230909/this-massive-streaming-stock-just-announced-a-10-for-1-stock-split-the-stock-is-up-26-this-year-and-wall-street-thinks-there-is-more-room-to-run)

`case_study:mercadolibre-2007-2025` · tickers US-MELI · confidence: verified

IPO Aug 10 2007 at $18 (first-day ~$27.62). Fell ~-88% in 2008 [unverified exact] amid the GFC and LatAm FX. Built Mercado Pago (payments, launched for marketplace buyers lacking cards/trust; later wallets, credit, merchant acquiring), Mercado Envios logistics (2013+) and ads. Stock ~$2,330 in Aug 2025 (+12,844% ≈ 130x since IPO, Motley Fool), peak ~$2,600 in 2025 [unverified]; ~$1,886 close on July 30 2026 (+6,728% vs first-day price). Split: mostly revenue/EPS growth (profitability arrived late, ~2020+); valuation stayed high on P/S. Drawdowns: ~-88% (2007-08); ~-67% (2021-22, ~$1,970 -> ~$600) [unverified]. EARLY SIGNAL visible ~2010-17: Mercado Pago total payment volume growing faster than marketplace GMV, increasingly off-platform — a fintech hidden inside an e-commerce stock; eBay had held ~19% from 2001 [unverified]. Who caught it: Baillie Gifford and other long-term growth funds [unverified in this pass]. Status: 2026 pullback on credit-book provisioning and competition (Shopee, Temu, Amazon) [unverified]. LESSON: in underpenetrated regions, the platform that also solves payments, logistics and trust builds a multi-sided moat; expect EM-style -70-90% drawdowns along the way.

- **Start → end:** $18 IPO → ~$2,330 (Aug 2025); ~$1,886 (Jul 2026) (~130x)
- **EPS vs rerating:** mostly revenue/EPS growth
- **Max drawdown:** ~-88% (2008) [unverified]; ~-67% (2021-22)
- **Early signal:** Mercado Pago TPV outgrowing GMV; logistics build
- **Who caught it:** eBay (early stake), Baillie Gifford [unverified]
- **Ended/stalled:** 2025 peak; 2026 pullback
- **Lesson:** multi-sided EM platform solving payments+logistics; survive EM drawdowns
- **Sources:** [1](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001099590/000119312508070409/d10k.htm) · [2](https://www.fool.com/investing/2025/08/17/prediction-buying-mercadolibre-could-set-you-life) · [3](https://www.fool.com/quote/NASDAQ/MELI) · [4](https://www.fool.com/investing/2025/03/15/think-too-late-mercadolibre-stock-still-time)

`insight:india-recovery-times` | confidence: **single-source** | tags: india, base-rate, cyclical

Approximate time for the Sensex/Nifty to regain a prior peak (levels and dates partly from memory; treat as indicative): 1992 peak 4,467 - exceeded by Sept 1994 (~2.5 years) but that 1994 high then capped the market for most of a decade; 2000 peak ~6,150 - regained around 2004-05 (~4-5 years); 2008 peak 21,206 - briefly regained Nov 2010 (~34 months), sustainably only late 2013 (~6 years of flat returns from the peak); 2015 peak ~30,000 - regained 2017 (~2 years); 2020 COVID crash - new high Nov 2020 (~8-10 months); Sept 2024 Nifty peak ~26,277 - Nifty touched a record 26,310 intraday on 27 Nov 2025 (~14 months) and was ~25,228 on 18 Nov 2026. Pattern: crashes caused by exogenous shocks with policy support (2020, 2016) recover in under a year; crashes after valuation-plus-credit booms (1992, 2000, 2008) take 4-6+ years for large caps and longer for the boom's leading sectors (capital goods 2007 -> ~2021; K-10 tech names never). Small caps take roughly 1.5-2x as long as large caps (see insight:smallcap-drawdown-durations). Implication: the cause of the fall (shock vs bubble unwind) is the best predictor of recovery time.

| key | value |
|---|---|
| shock_recovery | <1 yr (2016, 2020) |
| bubble_recovery | 4-6+ yrs (1992, 2000, 2008) |
| 2024_peak | regained Nov 2025 (~14 months) |

Links: case_study:capital-goods-2007 (about); event:ketan-parekh-tech-2000 (about)

`person:group-gvk` · flag: **poor** · confidence: verified · tickers: GVKPIL

Flag: POOR. Hyderabad infrastructure group that controlled Mumbai International Airport (MIAL, 50.5%) and Bangalore airport, plus power and roads, carrying group debt reported around Rs 32,000 cr (mid-2010s). Sold Bangalore airport stakes to Fairfax (33% in 2016, residual 10% for ~Rs 1,290 cr in 2017) to service debt -- the crown jewels went to lenders' needs rather than to shareholders. Allegations: CBI registered a case (27-Jun-2020) against chairman GVK Reddy, son G.V. Sanjay Reddy, MIAL and others alleging ~Rs 705 cr siphoned from MIAL -- ~Rs 310 cr via bogus works contracts with nine companies (2017-18) and ~Rs 395 cr of MIAL's surplus funds used for group companies (2012-2017); ED followed with a PMLA case. These are FIR allegations; no conviction or final finding was found in this scan. In 2020-21 Adani took control of MIAL by acquiring GVK's stake and debt; GVK Power & Infrastructure's listed shares became a penny stock. Early signals: holdco debt far above holdco cash flow, airport SPV surpluses moving to group companies, stake sales of the best assets, auditor qualifications on going concern. Lesson: when a group's only cash-generating asset is a regulated SPV with outside partners (AAI, ACSA, Bidvest), watch the SPV's related-party contracts.

- **allegations:** CBI FIR 2020 ~Rs 705 cr MIAL siphoning (pending)
